mike_sales: FYI Acme asked for a capacity plan for their enterprise reservation — want guidance on reserved GPUs + autoscale policy + worst-case eviction/fallback. Targets: steady ~1k RPS baseline, peaks to ~6k RPS for 1-3m bursts, latency p95 <250ms. Can we get back quick numbers and prewarm suggestions? cc @anya_se @pranay_infra
anya_se: quick Q — do we have avg token counts for their flows? that drives tokens/sec calc. I can map RPS->tokens then to GPU throughput.
mike_sales: they sent an excerpt: avg input ~60 tokens, avg output ~160 tokens. Mostly short chat completions (parallel). Daily 1.2M req, typical peak 500 rps, but bursts to 6k. pricing intent: reserved + burst credits. they asked about KV warmup strategy too.
pranay_infra: high-level: for steady 1k rps reserve a small pool; for bursts use autoscale up to target with burst credits. ballpark throughput (our gen-model, fp16): A100/A6000 equiv yields ~200k-300k tokens/sec depending on sequence length & batching. rough plan: reserve 2-3 gpus for steady ~1k, autoscale to ~5-7 gpus for 6k bursts to meet p95 targets. use quantized model variant as graceful degrade if nodes get evicted. also recommend prewarm windows and KV seeding.
anya_se: doing tokens math: PeakTokensPerSec = 6000 * (60+160) = 1,320,000 tokens/sec. If a single optimized GPU handles ~250k tokens/sec then GPUs_needed = ceil(1,320,000 / 250,000) = ~6. so 6 GPUs for strict p95 under bursts, matches pranay's 5-7 range.
anya_se: quick sim snippet I ran:
```
# rough sim (bash)
rps=6000
avg_tokens=220
tokens_per_sec=$((rps*avg_tokens))
gpu_tokens=250000
gpus=$(( (tokens_per_sec + gpu_tokens -1)/gpu_tokens ))
echo $gpus  # ~6
```
elaine_cust_success: on pricing/contract side: recommend proposing Reserved 3 GPUs + burst-to-6 GPU with burst credits. keeps commit lower and preserves headroom. I'll draft a cost example. also they left security questions: need confirmation on KMS, SOC2, data residency, and customer-managed keys. can product provide KMS integration blurb?
mike_sales: they also asked about autoscale cooldowns — if we spin up to hit a 3m burst, don't want thrash. suggested cooldown 10m and hold extra capacity 15m post-peak. thoughts?
pranay_infra: agree on cooldown 10m min, hold 15m to let KV cache stay hot. set max_batch_delay low (<=5ms) to protect p95. for KV warmup: pre-seed top N prefixes (recommend top 5k) before expected windows; provide a cache snapshot tool to restore during failover. eviction/fallback plan: if reserved pool nodes get preempted, route to quantized int8 variant on remaining nodes + fallback to hosted small-model endpoint with degraded latency but preserved availability. document the degrade path in runbook.
anya_se: action items: I'll produce a one-pager with numeric sizing (steady vs peak GPUs), tokens math, latency tradeoffs, and suggested autoscale policy. Elaine — can you own the security questionnaire answers (KMS + residency) and add the pricing example? Pranay — can you validate A100 vs A6000 throughput numbers and write the eviction fallback steps by EOD?
elaine_cust_success: on it. I'll draft answers and ping product for KMS snippet. ballpark cost estimate will be included (reserved 3 GPU + burst to 6 = ballpark $X/mo, will replace X with exact numbers once finance confirms).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: throughput-sim job complete for model 'gpt-compat-sim' — results: p95=230ms @4 GPUs, p95=190ms @6 GPUs (prod config). logs: https://internal/redwood/sim/1749971234
mike_sales: perfect. let's do a short sync 11:30am PST to lock the one-pager and questionnaire. if someone can't make, pls drop notes here.
anya_se: 11:30 works for me, will bring draft. :thumbsup:
pranay_infra: i'll join and bring the fallback runbook bullets. :+1:
elaine_cust_success: i'll be there with the security draft. :eyes:
